title: The Vijayanagara Empire
subtitle: The great south Indian empire of Hampi · 1336 – 1646
subject: vijayanagara-empire
intro: Founded on the banks of the Tungabhadra in 1336, Vijayanagara grew into the dominant power of south India for over two centuries. Its capital at Hampi, which foreign visitors compared to Rome, was one of the largest cities in the world. Ruled by four successive dynasties, the empire reached its height under Krishnadevaraya, was shattered at Talikota in 1565, and lingered on further south until the 1640s; its governors, the Nayaks and Wodeyars, inherited its lands.

events.title: Founding of Vijayanagara
events.summary: The brothers Harihara I and Bukka Raya I of the Sangama family found a kingdom on the Tungabhadra, in the wake of the Delhi Sultanate's raids into the south. Tradition credits the sage Vidyaranya of Sringeri with guiding them; 18 April 1336 is the traditional founding date.

events.title: Hoysala lands absorbed
events.summary: After the last Hoysala king is killed fighting the Madurai Sultanate, Vijayanagara takes over the old Hoysala territory and becomes the leading power south of the Krishna.

events.title: Bahmani Sultanate founded
events.summary: Rebel officers of the Delhi Sultanate found the Bahmani Sultanate at Gulbarga. For the next 150 years the two states fight repeatedly over the fertile Raichur Doab between the Krishna and Tungabhadra rivers.

events.title: Kumara Kampana conquers Madurai
events.summary: Bukka's son Kumara Kampana destroys the Madurai Sultanate and extends Vijayanagara rule to the far south. His wife Gangadevi celebrates the campaign in the Sanskrit poem Madhura Vijayam.

events.title: Harihara II takes the imperial title
events.summary: Bukka's son Harihara II is the first ruler to style himself emperor, reflecting a kingdom that now spans most of the peninsula.

events.title: Deva Raya II — the Sangama peak
events.summary: Deva Raya II modernises the army, recruiting Turkish archers and cavalry, and patronises Kannada and Telugu literature. Visitors describe a vast, wealthy capital.

events.title: Niccolò de' Conti visits
events.summary: The Venetian traveller Niccolò de' Conti describes the city's great circuit of walls and its huge population.

events.title: Abdur Razzaq's account
events.summary: The Persian envoy Abdur Razzaq writes that Vijayanagara had no equal in the world for its size and its markets.

events.title: Saluva Narasimha takes the throne
events.summary: After decades of weak Sangama rulers and losses to the Gajapatis of Odisha and the Bahmanis, the general Saluva Narasimha seizes power, founding the short-lived Saluva dynasty.

events.title: The Bahmani Sultanate breaks up
events.summary: The Bahmani state splits into five Deccan sultanates — Bijapur, Ahmadnagar, Golconda, Bidar and Berar — whose rivalries Vijayanagara exploits for decades.

events.title: Tuluva dynasty
events.summary: Vira Narasimha Raya founds the Tuluva dynasty, the third to rule Vijayanagara.

events.title: Krishnadevaraya crowned
events.summary: Krishnadevaraya begins a 20-year reign remembered as the empire's golden age — undefeated in battle, a poet himself, and a great builder.

events.title: Portuguese take Goa
events.summary: Afonso de Albuquerque captures Goa from Bijapur. Vijayanagara and the Portuguese become trading partners; Portuguese-supplied Arabian and Persian horses are vital to Vijayanagara's cavalry.

events.title: War with the Gajapatis
events.summary: Krishnadevaraya takes the Gajapati strongholds of Udayagiri and Kondaveedu and pushes north to the Godavari. Peace is sealed by his marriage to a daughter of Prataparudra Gajapati.

events.title: Building at Hampi and Tirumala
events.summary: Krishnadevaraya adds great gateway towers and halls to the Virupaksha Temple and other shrines at Hampi, and makes rich gifts to the Tirumala temple — monuments of Vijayanagara architecture.

events.title: Battle of Raichur
events.summary: Krishnadevaraya defeats Ismail Adil Shah of Bijapur and captures the fortress of Raichur, ending the long contest for the Raichur Doab in Vijayanagara's favour. Portuguese mercenaries fight on his side.

events.title: Domingo Paes describes the capital
events.summary: The Portuguese visitor Domingo Paes writes that the city is as large as Rome and very beautiful — the most detailed eyewitness description of Hampi at its height.

events.title: Court of the Ashtadiggajas
events.summary: Krishnadevaraya writes the Telugu poem Amuktamalyada and gathers the 'eight elephants' of Telugu poetry, the Ashtadiggajas, led by Allasani Peddana. Popular tradition adds the witty Tenali Rama. Kannada, Tamil and Sanskrit writers are also patronised.

events.title: Vyasatirtha and Purandara Dasa
events.summary: The philosopher Vyasatirtha, Krishnadevaraya's spiritual adviser, inspires the Haridasa movement. His disciple Purandara Dasa is later honoured as the father of Carnatic music.

events.title: Krishnadevaraya dies
events.summary: His half-brother Achyuta Deva Raya succeeds him and holds the empire together amid factional strife.

events.title: Fernão Nunes's chronicle
events.summary: The Portuguese horse trader Fernão Nunes writes a history of the kings of Vijayanagara.

events.title: Sadasiva Raya enthroned; Rama Raya rules
events.summary: Sadasiva Raya becomes emperor, but real power passes to Krishnadevaraya's son-in-law Aliya Rama Raya. He plays the Deccan sultanates against each other, intervening in their wars.

events.title: Battle of Talikota
events.summary: Bijapur, Ahmadnagar, Golconda and Bidar unite against Rama Raya. The Vijayanagara army is defeated, the elderly Rama Raya is captured and beheaded, and the army collapses. Also known as the battle of Rakkasa-Tangadi.

events.title: Sack of Hampi
events.summary: The victors plunder and burn the undefended capital for months. The city is abandoned; its ruins survive today as Hampi, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

events.title: Aravidu dynasty at Penukonda
events.summary: Rama Raya's brother Tirumala Deva Raya moves the court to Penukonda and founds the Aravidu dynasty, the fourth and last.

events.title: Venkatapati Raya's revival
events.summary: Venkatapati Raya restores some of the empire's strength and moves the capital further south to Chandragiri.

events.title: Raja Wodeyar takes Srirangapatna
events.summary: Raja Wodeyar of Mysore takes Srirangapatna from Vijayanagara's viceroy — the Mysore kingdom begins its rise as one of the empire's successor states.

events.title: Battle of Toppur — civil war
events.summary: After Venkatapati's death, rival claimants and the Nayaks fight a succession war. The empire's authority over its governors never recovers.

events.title: The Nayaks become kings
events.summary: The Nayaks of Madurai, Thanjavur, Gingee and Keladi — originally Vijayanagara governors — rule as independent kings, continuing its style of courts and temples.

events.title: Madras granted to the English
events.summary: Francis Day of the East India Company obtains a strip of coast from a local Nayak under the Vijayanagara emperor Venkata III. Fort St. George is built there — the origin of Chennai.

events.title: End of the empire
events.summary: Bijapur and Golconda overrun the last Vijayanagara territories. Sriranga III, the last emperor, spends his final years as a fugitive.

events.title: The Marathas in the old Vijayanagara lands
events.summary: Bijapur's campaigns in the former Vijayanagara lands bring Shahaji Bhosale south, with a jagir at Bangalore. In 1675 his son Ekoji takes Thanjavur from its Nayaks, founding the Thanjavur Maratha line.
